healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Sweden. Emergency number (112), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.

recommended: Tick-borne encephalitis (for summer hiking in endemic areas)
FSME (for Åland Islands and coastal areas during summer)
vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for travelers from any country. COVID-19 requirements vary — check current entry requirements. TBE (tick-borne encephalitis) is a risk for hikers in southern Sweden and Åland Islands during summer months (May-October). Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 9am-8pm Mon-Fri, 10am-6pm Sat, 11am-6pm Sun; some 24-hour pharmacies in major cities; chains include Apoteket, Apotek Hjärtat, and LloydsApotek
pharmacy.tips: Many common OTC medications available. Pharmacists are helpful and knowledgeable. Some US brand names may not be available — bring your preferred medications with generic names. Self-care for minor ailments is encouraged in Sweden. 1177.se provides health advice.

water.notes: Tap water is safe and of excellent quality throughout Sweden. It comes from protected sources and is among the cleanest in the world. Bottled water is unnecessary — bring a reusable bottle. Freshwater lakes and streams in pristine areas are generally safe to drink from.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Sweden has very high food safety standards. All food sold commercially is safe. Traditional Swedish cuisine (gravlax, meatballs, surströmming) from restaurants is safe. Be cautious with self-caught fish in areas with environmental advisories. Midsummer food from restaurants is safe.

travelInsurance.tips: Healthcare in Sweden is expensive for non-residents. A doctor visit costs $100-250+, specialist visits $200-400+, hospital stays $1,000-2,500+/day. Travel insurance with medical coverage is strongly recommended. EU/EEA citizens should carry their European Health Insurance Card (EHIC). Medical evacuation from remote northern areas (Lapland, mountain trails) can be very expensive.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Sweden has an excellent, well-organized healthcare system. Primary care (vårdcentraler) available throughout the country; hospitals in all major cities. English is universally spoken by medical staff. Pharmacies (apotek) are well-stocked with knowledgeable pharmacists.

medications.prescriptionRules: A valid prescription (Swedish or EEA prescription) is required for prescription medications. EEA prescriptions may be recognized for EU/EEA citizens. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances (narcotics class A/B). Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs. May need a permit from the Swedish Medical Products Agency (Läkemedelsverket) for larger quantities.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Some products may be available with prescription. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Swedish customs can be strict — declare all medications.

scams.name: Petition Pickpocket Scam
scams.description: Groups approach with charity petitions in Gamla Stan while accomplices pickpocket your bags.
scams.avoidance: Decline petition requests. Keep bags zipped and in front.

scams.name: Kronor Confusion
scams.description: Vendors give change in lower-value coins exploiting unfamiliarity with Swedish currency.
scams.avoidance: Use cards when possible — Sweden is largely cashless.

scams.name: Fake Accommodation
scams.description: Fraudulent listings for apartments that don't exist. Money collected upfront.
scams.avoidance: Book through platforms with buyer protection. Verify with Google Maps.

connectivity.simOptions: Telia, Tele2, or Tre prepaid SIMs at Pressbyrån kiosks or phone shops. eSIM via Airalo or Holafly. EU roaming with any EU SIM.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Excellent free WiFi everywhere — cafes, restaurants, public transport, and many public spaces. Sweden is one of the most connected countries.
connectivity.bestOption: EU SIM with roaming if you have one. Otherwise Airalo eSIM. Sweden is almost cashless — bring cards, not cash.

cultural.tipping: Not expected — service included in prices. Rounding up the bill is appreciated but not required. 5-10% at restaurants for exceptional service.
cultural.dressCode: Smart casual. Swedes dress stylishly but understated. No specific religious dress codes. Bring layers — weather changes quickly.
cultural.greetings: Handshake with eye contact. Swedes value personal space. First names used from the start. 'Hej' (hey) is the universal casual greeting.
taboos: Bragging or showing off (Jantelagen — 'don't think you're special')
Sitting next to someone on public transport when other seats are available
Small talk with strangers (less common than in other cultures)
cultural.haggling: Never. Prices are always fixed. Sweden is essentially cashless — card/mobile payment everywhere.

safety.lgbtSafety: Sweden is one of the most LGBTQ+-friendly countries in the world. Same-sex marriage has been legal since 2009, and comprehensive anti-discrimination laws are in place. Stockholm has a vibrant LGBTQ+ scene and Pride is widely celebrated nationwide.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Sweden is very safe for solo female travelers. Cities are well-lit and public transport is reliable and safe. Normal precautions apply in nightlife areas of Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö — drink spiking has been occasionally reported.
safety.notes: Sweden is a very safe country overall, though gang-related gun violence in certain suburban areas of Stockholm, Gothenburg, and Malmö has increased in recent years — these incidents do not target tourists. Pickpocketing occurs in Stockholm's tourist areas and on public transport. Sweden is nearly cashless — carry cards, not cash.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: 90 days visa-free (Schengen). UK, EU, Australia, Canada, Japan also visa-free.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: June-August (warm, midnight sun in the north). December-February for Northern Lights and snow activities. May and September for fewer crowds.

hospitals.name: Karolinska University Hospital
hospitals.notes: Sweden's leading university hospital. English spoken by virtually all medical staff.

hospitals.name: Sahlgrenska University Hospital
hospitals.notes: Major hospital serving Gothenburg and western Sweden.

immediate: Monitor SMHI (Swedish Meteorological Institute) storm warnings
Avoid unnecessary travel during Orange or Red weather warnings
In blizzard: do not leave vehicle if stranded — stay inside and call 112
Carry emergency winter kit in car: blanket, warm clothing, water
after: Check roof and structures for snow loading after heavy snowfall
Clear exits from buildings if snow blocks doors

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 112)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (112) and ambulance (112) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
